review.use_summary: Annotated genomic locations of ChIP-seq peaks with ChIPseeker 1.26.2, defining promoters from 2 kb upstream to 1 kb downstream of the transcription start site.
review.implementation_scope_note: The GRCh38 ChIP-seq analysis reports the 1.26.2 edition and -2 kb/+1 kb promoter definition, but not the precise TxDb/annotation resource, remaining annotation arguments or feature priorities. The original 1.26.2 adapter supports this explicit promoter window and genomic labels on a caller-supplied matching TxDb; the native prepared method separately audits nearest TSS assignments. No unreported settings are inferred, and differential binding, normalization and the complete ChIP_Zwart pipeline are not reproduced.

review.use_summary: Used ChIPseeker 1.34.1 for the genomic-location strategy linking TE-derived candidate cis-regulatory elements to genes within 3 kb flanking regions; cCRE-gene correlation was a separate strategy.
review.implementation_scope_note: The precise ChIPseeker function, gene/TxDb resource and anchor/orientation of the 3 kb flanks are unstated. The exact 1.34.1 adapter exposes original annotation and flanking-gene options, but this description does not identify a particular tssRegion, all-neighbor rule or nearest-gene-only call. Expression filtering, Wilcoxon accessibility testing, cCRE-gene correlation and HOMER enrichment remain separate analyses. Caller choices and original failures stay explicit.

review.use_summary: Annotated the genomic distribution of CUT&Tag peaks with ChIPseeker 1.22.1 after mm10 alignment and MACS2 peak calling.
review.implementation_scope_note: The paper reports ChIPseeker 1.22.1 and mm10 alignment, but omits the exact TxDb/resource, function, promoter window, gene-versus-transcript level and feature priorities. The original 1.22.1 adapter can produce genomic labels and distribution tables from explicit matching inputs; those unknown preparation/options are not inferred. Figure pixels and the full CUT&Tag pipeline are not reproduced.

review.use_summary: Used ChIPseeker to annotate genomic regions and retrieve the nearest gene around each ATAC-seq peak in the hg38 analysis; peak calling, union-peak counting and DESeq2 testing were separate steps.
review.implementation_scope_note: The ChIPseeker edition, exact hg38 annotation/TxDb resource, gene-versus-transcript level, distance/strand/overlap options and promoter window are unstated. The adapter requires an explicit supported edition and caller-supplied database; original genomic labels and nearest results are retained, with a separate scoped native nearest audit. Peak calling, union-peak count construction and DESeq2 inference are separate and are not supplied by this annotation command.

review.use_summary: Annotated ATAC-seq peaks with ChIPseeker using hg38 GENCODE version 30 annotations after the reported alignment, filtering, peak-calling and DESeq2 workflow.
review.implementation_scope_note: GENCODE v30 is the annotation release, not the ChIPseeker software version. The software edition, TxDb preparation, gene-versus-transcript level, promoter window and remaining arguments are unstated. The original annotation adapter requires the caller to preserve the hg38/GENCODE v30 resource identity and declare an edition/settings; native nearest mapping alone does not construct that annotation population. The upstream ATAC, count and differential-testing pipeline is not reproduced.

review.use_summary: Applied ChIPseeker annotatePeak with TxDb.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg19.knownGene annotations to retain enhancers for caQTL/no-effect SNP sets. Separately sampled 25,000 reference peaks and retained distal/intron categories, yielding approximately 21,000 putative reference enhancers.
review.implementation_scope_note: The exact ChIPseeker edition, annotation-package release, annotatePeak options and precise enhancer mask for the caQTL/no-effect sets are unstated. The adjacent paragraph specifies distal/intron categories for the separate random-reference enhancer set; do not silently transfer that mask or infer exact software label strings for every set. The adapter retains original annotations and supports caller-declared literal prefix selection, with no invented enhancer rule. Posterior thresholds, SNP-to-peak-center distance, matched downsampling and correlation are separate analyses.

supporting_evidence.relation_note: The adjacent paragraph continues enhancer categorization in the same Methods section and specifies the random-reference selection. It does not establish that the same mask applies to every caQTL/no-effect set.

review.use_summary: Analyzed Hi-C loop-anchor coordinates with ChIPseeker using the reported UCSC.hg38.knownGene annotations after Juicer contact-map processing and resolution/long-range-contact quality checks.
review.implementation_scope_note: The software edition, exact annotation package/release, function, gene-versus-transcript level and promoter/priorities are unstated. Preserve the reported UCSC.hg38.knownGene label without inventing a more specific package identity. Original annotation of explicit prepared anchors and a matching caller-supplied TxDb is available; Juicer contact-map processing, QC and prior-method domain/boundary/loop/compartment calling remain separate. This adapter does not call Hi-C loops or reconstruct those pipelines.
